lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6 you met the area of a triangle. What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm? Half of 6 × 4: 12 cm².
Three lengths make a triangle only if the two shorter sides add up to more than the longest: 3, 4 and 5 work; 2, 3 and 8 don't.
A triangle's angles add up to 180°. Given two angles, the third is fixed: 90° and 35° leave 55°.
Given three sides, only one triangle can be drawn; given three angles, many triangles (of different sizes) can.
Slicing a solid makes a flat cross-section: a cube sliced parallel to a face gives a square; a cylinder sliced across gives a circle.
Try it in the world: build a triangle of blocks with sides 3, 4 and 5 blocks. Then try 2, 3 and 8: can the ends meet? Next: angle facts.

exercises.prompt: Sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm can make a triangle.
A triangle has angles of 90° and 35°. What is the third angle, in degrees?
A cylinder is sliced parallel to its base. What shape is the cut?
exercises.explain: A circle, like cutting a log straight across.

exercises.prompt: Sides of 2 cm, 3 cm and 8 cm can make a triangle.
How many different triangles can you draw with sides 5, 6 and 7 cm?
exercises.explain: Just one: three sides fix the triangle's shape and size.

exercises.prompt: How many triangles have angles 50°, 60° and 70°?
exercises.explain: Many: the angles fix the shape but not the size.

exercises.prompt: A square-based pyramid is sliced parallel to its base. What is the cut?
exercises.explain: A square: every slice parallel to the base has the base's shape, and the slices shrink as they rise to the point, so it is a smaller square.

exercises.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40°. What is each base angle, in degrees?
exercises.explain: The angles add up to 180°, so the two base angles share 180 − 40 = 140°. They are equal, so each is 140 ÷ 2 = 70°. Check: 40 + 70 + 70 = 180.

exercises.prompt: Sort the side lengths: can they make a triangle?
exercises.hint: Add the two shorter sides. Is the sum more than the longest?
exercises.explain: 3 + 4 > 5, 5 + 5 > 5 and 6 + 8 > 10: triangles. 2 + 3 < 8 and 1 + 2 < 4: the ends can't meet.

exercises.prompt: Match each solid and slice to the cross-section.
exercises.hint: Picture the flat face the cut makes.
exercises.explain: A cube cut parallel to a face gives a square; a cylinder cut across gives a circle; a square pyramid cut across gives a smaller square.

exercises.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm. What is the longest whole number of centimetres the third side can be?
exercises.hint: The two shorter sides must add up to more than the longest. What if the third side is the longest?
exercises.explain: If the third side is the longest, the other two must add up to more than it: 7 + 10 = 17, so it must be less than 17 cm. The longest whole number is 16 cm. Check: 17 is more than 16, so the ends meet.
